sections.h2: Why does the city inspection decide how an Allen Park sale goes?
sections.html:
Because an Allen Park house cannot close without a Certificate of Occupancy or a signed buyer affidavit, and getting either takes days. The rule covers homes first listed on or after March 1, 2022, under Chapter 10, Article 10, Section 10-404 of the city code.

Plan the order of events around it. Book the inspection as soon as you decide to sell, read the report, and decide whether to repair the cited items or sell with the buyer taking them on. Skipping this step is the usual reason a sale to a cash buyer in Allen Park slips past its scheduled closing date.

sections.h2: How does the Allen Park sales inspection work?
sections.html:
The Building Department walks the interior and the outside of the lot, and the fee of $175 pays for both the first visit and the follow-up. The city publishes a list of the most common violations and an application form, so you can check your own house before the inspector arrives.

  • Fix every cited item and the department issues the Certificate of Occupancy.
  • Or sell as is, which requires the buyer to sign an affidavit accepting the violations.
  • The buyer also puts at least $500 into escrow, and 10 percent of it cannot be refunded.
  • That affidavit takes the place of the certificate as the closing document.
  • Reports can be mailed or picked up within 5 business days of the inspection.

Phone the Building Department at 313-928-4441 or 313-928-4134 to schedule. The city's advice to sellers is plain: do not set a closing date until you hold the certificate or the buyer's signed affidavit.

sections.h2: What is Allen Park like as a place to sell?
sections.html:
Allen Park is a small Downriver city, 7.00 square miles of land, about 12 miles from downtown Detroit. Ford offices and facilities sit inside it, the Detroit Lions train and keep their headquarters here, and the Uniroyal Giant Tire, a former World's Fair Ferris wheel moved to the city in 1966, is its best-known landmark.

A village from 1927 and a city since 1957, Allen Park took its name from a lawyer and lumberman who held land across what is now Allen Park and Melvindale. Its population leaped from 12,329 in 1950 to 37,494 in 1960 and topped out at 40,747 in 1970, which is why so many of its brick houses date from the postwar boom. The 2020 count was 28,638, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 27,445.

Neighbors on the map are Dearborn, Dearborn Heights, Melvindale, Lincoln Park, Southgate and Taylor. I-94 crosses the north end, I-75 clips the southeast corner, and Southfield Road (M-39) slices through as an eight-lane boulevard. The Fairlane Green shopping center opened in 2006, and the city once earned a spot on a magazine's list of top small cities.

Bowlers know the city too: Thunderbowl Lanes hosted the 2009 PBA World Series of Bowling. In 1950 the area directly west of Melvindale still belonged to Ecorse Township, a reminder that the city's current shape came together in stages after incorporation.

sections.h2: Which school district does an Allen Park address belong to?
sections.html:
It depends on the street. Most of the city sits in the Allen Park School District, which runs Arno, Lindemann and Bennie elementary schools plus Allen Park Middle School and Allen Park High School. The north end is part of Melvindale-Northern Allen Park Public Schools, and the area south of the Sexton-Kilfoil Drain falls in the Southgate Community School District.

Allen Park High School opened in 1950, and before that local students finished the eighth grade at Lapham school and then traveled to other cities for high school. Inter-City Baptist School and the St. Frances Cabrini schools, including Cabrini High School, are the local private options. Put the district name in your listing, since families shopping by school will filter by it.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Allen Park homes and households?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 figures describe a stable, owner-heavy suburb. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $183,700, and renters are a small minority.

In the 2020 census, 12,252 housing units stood in the city and only 3.8 percent were vacant. About 30 percent of households were one person living alone, and the median age was 41.5.

Daily life figures round out the picture. Workers average a 23.8 minute trip to work, 66.1 percent of residents over 16 are in the labor force, and 31.0 percent of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree. The poverty rate is 6.9 percent, 91.1 percent of households have broadband, and the city counts 1,301 veterans, which is useful context for a seller wondering who the local buyers are.

sections.h2: What does Wayne County charge to record an Allen Park deed?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30 per document, split as $26 for the register plus a $4 state survey and remonumentation fee. That schedule started January 1, 2026, the first increase at the office since 1996.

Transfer tax is collected when the deed is recorded: $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state. For a house that sells at $185,000 the combined tax is $1,591, and the seller bears it. Warranty deeds must carry a certification from the Wayne County Treasurer before they are recorded.

Payment rules at the Register of Deeds are stricter than at many counties:

  • Cards are taken at the counter with matching ID, but never by mail.
  • Personal checks are taken by mail only, not at the counter.
  • American Express and Discover are refused.
  • Each document needs its own check for the exact amount, and a check more than $25 too high sends the papers back.

The office answers questions at (313) 224-5851.

sections.h2: Why does the Wayne County Register of Deeds reject deeds?
sections.html:
Most rejections come from a short list of mistakes. Copies in place of original signatures are refused, and so is a deed that states neither a price nor an exemption statute. Other common problems are a legal description that is incomplete, a missing property tax ID number or address, a notary block that is unclear, and a missing return-to name and address.

When several documents share a single check, one bad document sends the whole bundle back. Have the drafter go through the checklist before closing day, and ask your title agent to confirm the tax certification is done.

sections.h2: What changes if the Allen Park house is a rental?
sections.html:
Every rental house must hold a Certificate of Compliance before anyone occupies it. Registration costs $200 at first, renewal costs $175, and each certificate lasts three years.

City rental inspectors work Tuesdays and Thursdays only, using the same Building Department phone numbers as the sales inspection. Landlords whose house is not rented can file a non-rental affidavit. If a tenant lives in the house when you sell, expect scheduling work for the interior inspection, and a buyer who will keep renting should ask for the date of your current certificate.

faqs.q: Does a house listed before March 1, 2022 need a Certificate of Occupancy?
faqs.a: No. The city exempts homes listed before that date, but homes listed on or after it need the certificate or a buyer's signed affidavit before closing.

faqs.q: What does the Allen Park inspection fee cover?
faqs.a: The $175 fee covers the initial inspection and the final one. Written reports are ready for mailing or pickup within 5 business days.

faqs.q: How is transfer tax figured on an Allen Park sale?
faqs.a: Multiply the price in thousands by $8.60, since the state takes $3.75 per $500 and the county takes $0.55 per $500. A $185,000 sale produces $1,591, owed by the seller.

faqs.q: Which county office records an Allen Park deed?
faqs.a: The Wayne County Register of Deeds. Its fee has been $30 per document since January 1, 2026, and the county treasurer certifies warranty deeds beforehand.

faqs.q: Can the house sell with open code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, as is. The buyer signs an affidavit taking on the violations and escrows at least $500, and the repairs happen after closing.
